s1.syndrome_frame: Subcutaneous mass in the lower abdominal region with cyclical pain
salient_findings: Subcutaneous nodule approximately 1 cm in diameter
key_facts: 39-year-old female patient
History of chronic urticaria
History of cesarean section eight years ago
History of myomectomy six months ago
Denies history of dysmenorrhea and abortion
Slight pain accompanying the mass
Pain worsens around menstruation
No palpable swelling of superficial lymph nodes
Linear scar in the lower-left abdominal region
Ultrasonography showed a hybrid echo-mass about 1.1 × 1.0 cm
Histopathology revealed endometrial glands and stroma

key_facts: 39-year-old female patient

Slight pain accompanying the mass

shortlist.label: Abdominal wall endometriosis
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology revealed endometrial glands and stroma, and the mass is accompanied by cyclical pain

shortlist.label: Endometrioma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of endometrial glands and stroma in the subcutaneous mass, and the patient's history of myomectomy

shortlist.label: Scar endometriosis
shortlist.why_kept: Linear scar in the lower-left abdominal region and the presence of endometrial glands and stroma in the mass

shortlist.label: Nodular fasciitis with endometrial-like features
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology revealed endometrial-like features, and the mass has a well-defined border

shortlist.label: Subcutaneous myoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of myomectomy and the presence of a subcutaneous mass with a well-defined border

raw.rationale: The patient's history of cesarean section and myomectomy, combined with the presence of a subcutaneous mass near the scar and histopathology revealing endometrial glands and stroma, support this diagnosis. The worsening of pain around menstruation also aligns with endometriosis.

rejected.label: Abdominal wall endometriosis
rejected.why: While possible, the specific location near a surgical scar and the patient's history of surgery make scar endometriosis more likely.

rejected.label: Endometrioma
rejected.why: Typically refers to an ovarian cyst related to endometriosis, which does not match the subcutaneous location of the mass in this case.

rejected.label: Nodular fasciitis with endometrial-like features
rejected.why: This condition does not typically present with a clear connection to menstrual cycles or prior surgical scars.

rejected.label: Subcutaneous myoma
rejected.why: The histopathology showing endometrial glands and stroma does not support a diagnosis of myoma, which would be expected to show smooth muscle cells instead.
